# `\` — Scan

`f\Y` scans left-to-right: each result becomes the next call's left argument.

```bpl
+\1 2 3            ⍝ 1 3 6
-\1 2 3            ⍝ 1 ¯1 ¯4
```

`S f\ Y` starts with seed `S`, excluding the seed from the result.

```bpl
10-\1 2 3          ⍝ 9 7 4
100+\10 20         ⍝ 110 130
```

The whole seed starts each lane. A scalar seed stands for its content, so `(⊂10)+\v` is `10+\v`. Use Rank for separate seeds per cell.

```bpl
M←[1 2 3 ⋄ 4 5 6]
10 20+\⍤0 1 M      ⍝ [11 13 16 ⋄ 24 29 35]
[10]+\1 2 3        ⍝ [[11] [13] [16]]
```

Empty scans and unseeded singletons make no calls. [Axis](axis.qmd) `⍠K` selects the axis, and [`⍀`](backslash-bar.qmd) defaults to the first.

```bpl
+\⍠0 [1 2 3 ⋄ 4 5 6]  ⍝ [1 2 3 ⋄ 5 7 9]
```

APL difference: every scan left-accumulates, including dfns.

## Errors

- `DOMAIN`: a subject operand. Expand with [`#⁻¹`](hash.qmd#expand)
